answer: Every agent identity must lock a deposit returned only after an epoch of peer-attested work, priced against live task fees. A Sybil swarm gets no shortcut: each clone needs its own funded stake before bidding, so minting ten thousand fakes costs ten thousand stakes rather than ten thousand free signups. The ledger is a prism splitting stake into penalties, so one bad clone burns its deposit and drags its sponsor down. Against saffron-cheap registration fees that price is brutal, while honest newcomers still climb in as each opal identity proves itself through work.
